chapter: Kenton, Granz, Parker and the jazz clubs
title: Rehearsing and recording with Parker
summary: Granz brought Parker to rehearse; Parker rejected Peanut Vendor and played Mango Mangue.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So how did you start playing with Parker? How did Parker start playing with Machito's band?

So after we marry, I really don't know exactly what brought us together. In the meantime Norman Granz came, and he had the band. And he said, man, I want to record this band. He came to me to -- would you like to record for me and so forth? You don't mind if I bring some solo with me. Then he had Flip Phillips and they contract with a jazz trombonist -- Charlie Parker -- so they brought Charlie to the Palladium.

So he had a band and so forth (inaudible). So we go rehearse. So when he came to rehearsal, said, you brought any kind of music. No, I -- he said, no, I ain't got no music (inaudible) we ain't prepared for you then. We ain't got nothing special for you to play. He said, no, no, never mind. Play me the -- anything that you have there.
I remember Norman Granz wanted him to play the Peanut Vendor. So I play "Peanut Vendor" for him. And Charlie (inaudible) he's saying --
And Charlie could play it too?
Yeah, he said, this ain't for me. He

said, you know, I'm -- he said, this number (inaudible) this number is (inaudible), and I don't want to touch nothing that'll conflict. You got anything else? Yeah. I tell you, I got -- I say, I've got a whole lot of numbers, but they -- you know, in Cuban music everything is vocal (inaudible). He said, I don't care. When the vocal is supposed to sing, you just cue me, and I'm coming in.
So I played an arrangement, GRACIRA sings 'Mango Mangue' (inaudible) bongo-bongo.

-- so we start again, and we get to the (inaudible) never mind the MONTUNO (inaudible), so he -- that was one of the first numbers (inaudible) Bongo-bongo. And then we create some number that -- he play (inaudible), and then we gave -- we draw some (inaudible), and then they start looking around, they start doing something with their mouth (inaudible) fool around, play like a bongo with the mouth, say (inaudible) and start improvising on top of that.

And, you know, the whole ATMOSPHERE (inaudible) begin to blend. Everything (inaudible). That's the way the thing operated. And then we went to the big scene, Chico wrote . They had this part (inaudible) for this particular -- East Side, it was more spontaneous noise.
